test_title: SSC CGL (2022) Tier-II Official Paper (Held On : 7 March 2023)
subject: general
question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 11?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number is divisible by 11 if |Sum of digits at odd positions − Sum of digits at even positions| is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Testing 5214341:

Sum of digits at odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th) = 5 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 10

Sum of digits at even positions (2nd, 4th, 6th) = 2 + 4 + 4 = 10

Difference = 10 − 10 = 0. Since the difference is 0, the number is divisible by 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 5214341.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Numbers: 5214341, 5648741, 6598321, 2378965

Divisibility Rule for 11: The difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places must be 0, 11, 22, 33, etc.

⇒ Option (1): 5214341

⇒ Sum of odd-position digits = 5 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 10

⇒ Sum of even-position digits = 2 + 4 + 4 = 10

⇒ Difference = 10 − 10 = 0 (Divisible by 11)

⇒ Option (2): 5648741

⇒ Sum of odd-position digits = 5 + 4 + 7 + 1 = 17

⇒ Sum of even-position digits = 6 + 8 + 4 = 18

⇒ Difference = |17 − 18| = 1 (Not divisible by 11)

⇒ Option (3): 6598321

⇒ Sum of odd-position digits = 6 + 9 + 3 + 1 = 19

⇒ Sum of even-position digits = 5 + 8 + 2 = 15

⇒ Difference = |19 − 15| = 4 (Not divisible by 11)

⇒ Option (4): 2378965

⇒ Sum of odd-position digits = 2 + 7 + 9 + 5 = 23

⇒ Sum of even-position digits = 3 + 8 + 6 = 17

⇒ Difference = |23 − 17| = 6 (Not divisible by 11)

**∴ The correct answer is 5214341.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 (or 9) if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 3 (or 9).

Divisibility by 7

Subtract twice the last digit from the number formed by the remaining digits; the result should be divisible by 7.

Divisibility by 13

Add four times the last digit to the number formed by the remaining digits; the result should be divisible by 13.

Divisibility by 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if the last 2 digits are divisible by 4, and by 8 if the last 3 digits are divisible by 8.</p
